main_interpretation.near: Balanced converts the signal (learned benefit AUC 0.805, regret 0.005), Precision does not (AUC 0.339). The signal is real but unstable and not converted to certified coverage.
main_interpretation.contact: Precision shows partial transferable benefit ranking (learned AUC 0.613, correlation 0.166), Balanced remains weak (AUC 0.432, correlation -0.165). The ability is partial and not jointly present with the strongest Near branch.
main_interpretation.harm: Broad harm AUC is about 0.60-0.66, but harmful top-1 switching remains 0.445-0.698, so the safety frontier is not solved.
main_interpretation.proposal: positive top-k oracle hit is approximately 0.97-1.00; proposal generation is not the bottleneck.
main_interpretation.certificate: all main and ablation verify coverage is zero.

root_defects: Raw benefit, component harm, and final safe admission were compressed into two learned hypotheses.
The v48.21 group MIL noisy-OR used opportunity probability only and ignored harm although the label meant safe opportunity.
Training, checkpointing, calibration, selector, and closed-loop did not share one explicit admission score.
Safe-admission gradients competed with raw-benefit semantics and caused complementary Balanced/Precision specialization.
Epoch-zero source/consensus identity was never eligible for checkpoint selection.
Global AUC diagnostics concealed failure among high-opportunity candidates.

v48_22_changes.mil: explicit admission probability; two-head ablation uses P(benefit)*(1-P(harm))
v48_22_changes.score_consistency: same admission score in loss, dev checkpointing, calibration, evaluation, selector, and closed-loop
